output.brief: The 2026 Pellacott VA-220 valves are defective: returned units show seat leakage from a deformed slide seal, and warehouse valves never installed fail a helium leak test at 11% (Pellacott 2025 1%, Durrant-Hale 0%). Installer firm and firmware version do not explain it: failure rates are similar across legacy and new installers and across 4.1 and 4.2. The bigger problem is the certificates. Leak rig LT-04, which the certificates cite, was out of service from 9 January 2026, no VA-220 test program is loaded on the other rigs, and the per-piece data repeats a few fixed sequences. The "perfect" scores therefore reflect records that were probably not produced by real tests. Pellacott's seal-source change is a plausible cause but is not yet proven, since it is confounded with the move to Line 3. Next steps: quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott VA-220 stock, including the six held lots, suspend its dock-to-stock status, and release only after Brenmoor-run helium testing. Do not release the held lots on Pellacott's new certificates, and do not penalise the installers. I am fairly confident in the defect and the certificate finding. I have not checked whether other suppliers' records are also fabricated.
